source_title: Comprehensive Sheep Production Guide — East Africa, Tanzania

chunks.text: Sheep breeds in Tanzania: Dorper — South African meat breed, white body with black head, excellent growth rate 200-300 g/day, mature ram 80-120 kg, ewe 60-80 kg, hair sheep (no shearing), good mothering ability, adapts well to tropical conditions, prolific (150-180% lambing rate). Red Maasai — indigenous East African breed, red/brown wool, hardy and trypanotolerant, adapted to humid coastal lowlands, mature ewe 30-40 kg, low growth rate 80-120 g/day, good disease resistance, twinning rate 10-15%. Black Head Persian — fat-tailed breed, black head with white body, mature ram 60-80 kg, ewe 45-60 kg, hair sheep, good heat tolerance, moderate growth rate. Local Tanzania breeds — small framed, 25-35 kg mature weight, varied colours, very hardy, low production but adapted to local conditions, used for meat and as foundation for upgrading programs.

Sheep reproduction: Oestrus cycle length 17 days (range 14-19), shorter than goats. Oestrus duration 24-36 hours. Signs of heat: restlessness, frequent urination, mounting other ewes, standing to be mounted, vulva swelling with clear mucus discharge, reduced appetite. Ram effect: introduction of a ram to anovulatory ewes can synchronize oestrus within 2-6 days. Gestation length 147 days (range 142-152), shorter than goats (150 days). Ram:ewe ratio for natural service: 1:25-30 for mature rams, 1:15-20 for young rams. Lambing management: prepare lambing pen 7 days before due date, ensure adequate colostrum within 2 hours (10% body weight in first 24 hours), check for multiple births, ensure all lambs suckle. Common lambing problems: oversized lambs (especially in crossbred ewes carrying single large lamb), uterine torsion, ringwomb (incomplete cervical dilation). Post-lambing care: check for retained placenta (normal expulsion within 6 hours), monitor for metritis (foul-smelling discharge, fever), ensure adequate milk production.

Sheep diseases specific to Tanzania: Ovine Progressive Pneumonia (OPP) — retrovirus causing chronic wasting, progressive pneumonia, hard udder (indurative mastitis), arthritis. No vaccine, no treatment, cull affected animals. Johne's disease (paratuberculosis) — Mycobacterium avium subsp paratuberculosis, chronic wasting despite adequate nutrition, profuse watery diarrhoea, bottle jaw, no treatment, cull, test and remove. Footscald — Fusobacterium necrophorum only (mild), interdigital dermatitis without underrun, treat with footbath (10% zinc sulphate), keep in dry area. Pregnancy toxaemia (twin lamb disease) — occurs in last 4-6 weeks of gestation carrying twins or triplets, energy deficit causes ketosis, signs: separation from flock, nervous signs, recumbency, death. Prevention: adequate nutrition in late gestation (increase concentrate by 50% for twin-bearers), treatment: oral propylene glycol 60ml twice daily, IV dextrose 40% 500ml, dexamethasone to induce parturition if ewe not responding. Pulpy kidney (Clostridium perfringens type D enterotoxaemia) — sudden death in rapidly growing lambs on good pasture, vaccination prevents (Clostridium C+D vaccine). Nasal bot fly (Oestrus ovis) — larvae in nasal sinuses, signs: nasal discharge, head shaking, snorting, treatment: Ivermectin 0.2mg/kg SC, or Doramectin 0.2mg/kg SC.

Sheep nutrition requirements: Dry matter intake 3-4% body weight for adult ewes, 4-5% for growing lambs. Late gestation ewe carrying twins: 14-16% crude protein, 2.8-3.0 Mcal/kg metabolizable energy, increase feed by 50% over maintenance. Lactating ewe: 12-14% CP, 2.6-2.8 Mcal/kg ME. Growing lamb: 14-16% CP, 2.8-3.0 Mcal/kg ME for optimal growth rate. Common feeds in Tanzania: Napier grass (10-14% CP), Rhodes grass (8-10% CP), Cynodon (8-9% CP), Desmodium (15-18% CP), Leucaena leaf meal (20-25% CP — limit to 30% of diet to avoid mimosine toxicity), maize bran (9% CP), cotton seed cake (25-30% CP), sunflower cake (30-35% CP). Mineral supplementation: provide free choice mineral lick or mineral block containing calcium, phosphorus, sodium, copper (goats and sheep have higher copper requirement than cattle but can be susceptible to copper toxicity — avoid copper oxide needles). Cobalt supplementation important in deficient areas (vitamin B12 injection or cobalt bullet). Selenium and Vitamin E for white muscle disease prevention (inject Dystosel at birth in deficient areas).

Lamb marking and management: Tail docking at 7-14 days using rubber ring (elastrator) or hot iron. Dock tails to 3-4 vertebrae (cover vulva in ewes, 2-3cm below tail head in rams). Castration at 7-14 days using rubber ring — note: rubber ring causes gradual ischaemic necrosis, takes 2-3 weeks for scrotum to fall off. Ear tagging or tattooing for identification at lamb marking. Ear tags: apply in middle of ear avoiding major blood vessels, use unique flock number. Vaccination at lamb marking: first Clostridial vaccine (C+D) at 8-10 weeks, booster at 12-14 weeks. Creep feeding: provide high-protein creep ration (18% CP) in creep area inaccessible to ewes from 2 weeks of age. Weaning: at 12-16 weeks or when lambs reach 15-20 kg. Post-weaning management: continue growing ration for 4-6 weeks, drench with anthelmintic, vaccinate, assess growth rate (target 150-250 g/day for Dorper crosses).

Sheep housing and management in Tanzania: Housing should provide shade, rain protection, and predator security. Minimum floor space: 1.0-1.5 sq meters per adult sheep. Floors: raised slatted floors preferred for parasite control, or deep litter with regular bedding changes. Ventilation: good airflow without drafts, especially important in humid coastal areas. Predator protection: secure fencing (woven wire 1.2m high with electric outrider), lock sheep in kraal at night. Flock management: separate ewes, rams, lambs, and dry stock. Ram management: run with ewes only during mating season (6-8 weeks), separate rest of year. Shearing: hair sheep breeds (Dorper, Black Head Persian) do not require shearing. Wool breeds: shear twice per year (before and after long rains). Hoof trimming: every 6-8 weeks, especially in wet conditions, trim to level walking surface, remove overgrown horn.
